differences.what: massing: a narrow, tall stone town house, its front flat, attached on the north to the Farwell house and open to the south, its south side wall receding along the open ground; the draft stood a grey mansard box 6.75 m wide
differences.how: T-2432: K01 frontage on the 1911 sheet's plan at the trace's own 7.6 m width; the front's two edges land within 3 px of the photograph's (x 140 and 433), the south wall recedes on the camera's solve

differences.what: storey lines and the north part's windows: three storeys, the ground floor near grade; ground-floor lights 1.1-2.7 m over grade, first-floor 4.15-6.4 m, second-floor 7.8-10.1 m, two a storey in the north part
differences.how: T-2432: a 0.45 m ground floor and 3.15, 3.6 and 3.8 m storeys; the north part's sills and heads fall within about 5 px of the photograph's, their columns within about 8 px

differences.what: the entrance at grade at the south end of the front, flat-headed, reached by two low steps, with one window a storey over it
differences.how: T-2432: the K07 door at front bay 5.75 m, three 0.15 m risers; its jambs within 5 px of the photograph's

differences.what: the gable: the photograph carries the whole front up as a steep coped WALL GABLE, about 57 degrees, its apex about 18.8 m over grade, three segment-headed lights in the attic at 11.6-13.4 m and an oculus near the apex; the build has a 45-degree slated hip and a single-light pedimented dormer on the front's centre line, its light at the gable lights' height and its apex about 4 m lower
differences.how: T-2730: the front carried up as K01's shaped-gable slab with a straight coped outline in the front's stone: the apex at 18.85 m within about 7 px of the photograph's, the rakes at 61 degrees against its 60-66, its south foot on the 13.0 m ledge where the corner pier's top stands; the three lights segment-headed one-over-one sash at 11.53-13.34 m, 0.94 m apart, within about 5 px of the photograph's; the oval light at 15.56 m in its stone ring with a cross of bars for its tracery. The gable stands on the front's centre line, about 0.3 m (12 px) south of the photograph's, and its face steps 0.25 m proud of the wall at 11.22 m, under the lights (L-k01-1625-mcbirney-wall-gable-2730)

differences.what: the south side wall's eave: the photograph's runs about 13 m over grade, a knee wall under the attic; the build's eave is the third floor's, 11.0 m
differences.how: T-2730: the wall head at 13.0 m, the second floor's storey carrying the knee wall (K01 has no attic storey), the eave plain at 0.05 m; the hip's ridge at 16.8 m behind the gable

differences.what: the windows' kind: the photograph's ground- and first-floor windows are leaded casements, two lights under a transom, mullioned, in dressed quoined surrounds; its second-floor windows single one-over-one sash under segmental heads, the middle one standing a little south of the windows under it; the build has K06 two-over-two sash under flat stone lintels, all on one bay line
differences.how: T-2752: each street window named off the photograph with its own centre, width, sill and head (street_front_windows) and glazed from new K06 kinds: the ground floor's two lights on a stone mullion, 1.19-2.59 m; the first floor's two lights under a transom about a third down, 4.14-6.40 m; the second floor's one-over-one segmental sash at 1.15 and 3.45 m, off the columns below as the print sets them; their edges within about 1-2 px of the print's. The glazing bars are the kit's: the print shows small panes and cannot say lead or wood

differences.what: the frontispiece: the front's south part stands slightly proud, its edges quoined, and the lower windows sit in dressed, quoined surrounds; the photograph has a carved panel over the door and a hood mould over the four-light window; the build lays the four-light mullioned and transomed window over the door and the two narrow segment-headed lights over it (T-2752) in the front's own plane, with no projection, quoins, panel or hood
differences.how: T-2753 (street_front_frontispiece): the front from s 3.81 m (x 287 px) to its south corner stands 0.10 m proud from grade to the hood mould, its coursing and the four-light window and door laid on that face; both arrises quoined 0.25 and 0.42 m in turn, the north column within about 2 px of the print's (x 287-298); the hood mould a weathered course at 7.05-7.30 m across the frontispiece's width, within about 3 px of the print's (y 513-523), 0.08 m past its face and north arris; the lower windows' and the four-light window's surrounds dressed jamb stones 0.18 and 0.30 m in turn under a 0.35 m dressed lintel course; the door in a 0.35 m dressed band with its lintel to 3.45 m and over it the carved panel, 0.83 m across at s 5.67 m (the print's x 343-375 px), a raised border and a raised oval cartouche standing for the carving. The projection's depth, the hood's overhang and the carving are reconstructed (L-k01-1625-mcbirney-frontispiece-2753); the panel is 0.51 m tall where the print's is 0.86 m, the door's height (below) leaving no more room

differences.what: the base: the photograph shows a plain plinth with no basement lights; the build has low area lights under the ground-floor windows, which a K01 front without its own openings row must carry
differences.how: T-2752: no basement light in the front; the plinth is the K02 base, its stone plain under the coping

differences.what: the plinth's height: the photograph's plain plinth band stands about 0.26 m over the walk (y 785 px); the build's K02 base and coping rise to 0.48 m, the least the K02 base lays (one 0.25 m course under the 0.23 m coping)

the belts: the photograph runs a string course under the first-floor windows at about 4.0 m and caps the frontispiece at about 7.2 m; the build carries K01's own belts at 3.40-3.60 and 7.05-7.20 m across the whole front
differences.how: T-2753 (street_front_windows.belts): one string course at 3.96-4.14 m across the whole front, in place of K01's two; within about 2 px of the print's line in the north part (y 637-643 px) and about 3 px under it on the frontispiece, whose face the print draws a little higher; the frontispiece's cap at about 7.2 m is the hood mould (above)

differences.what: the door's height: the print's door opening stands about 0.13-2.64 m over grade (y 693 px at its head), its surround's lintel to about 3.11 m and the carved panel 3.16-4.02 m; the build's K07 door stands on the 0.45 m ground floor to a head at 3.15 m, about 20 px higher, so its surround's lintel rises to 3.45 m and the panel between that and the string course is 0.51 m tall
the second floor's segmental heads: the photograph's rise about 0.19 m on a 0.94 m span (about a fifth); K06's working segmental rise is an eighth of the span, 0.12 m, about 3 px lower at the crown
the stacks: the photograph's tall stack stands on the north party wall near the front, beside the gable; the build's stands 9.4 m behind the front (a K01 stack may not stand in the dormer's body)
differences.how: T-2730: the tall stack on the north party wall about 1.6 m behind the gable's face, solved through the camera from its edges (x 180 and 217 px), 1.0 m along the front and its top at 17.7 m, within about 6 px of the photograph's; built 0.3 m in from the party wall, the K01 rule for a stack in a hip

differences.what: the four-storey rear section: the photograph shows it stepping out to the south behind the main body under a mansard with a dormer and a stack, as the 1911 sheet traces it (s20-1625-a1); not built, a K01 rear wing standing only behind the main body inside its width
differences.how: T-2820 (rear_section): the step-out 1.3 m past the south wall over the rear 7.6 m, in the K03 brick to the main wall head, its street face with the print's door at its foot and one window a storey (3.66-6.65 and 9.02-11.48 m, read against the cornice where it meets the main eave, y 482-488 px); over the rear part an attic of its own, its steep slated faces to a curb at 17.3 m (the print's top line, y 392 px), the gabled dormer on its street face (sill 13.85 m, sash head 16.3 m), the south end wall carried up its outline as a coped parapet to the rear stack, which tops at 19.6 m; the main roof's ridge dies into the attic's street face (L-k01-1625-rear-section-2820)

differences.what: the rear section's street face: the print's reads about 50 px across (x 528-577), its corner with the main south wall at x 528 and its lit south end at x 577-610, the stack at x 580-602; on the camera's solve the sheet's 1.3 m step stands at x 505-527, so the face is about 20 px narrower than the print's and stands about 25 px north of it, its windows (0.75 m, the contract's narrowest sash) and dormer narrower with it. No camera that fits the front can stand a 1.3 m face 50 px wide that far back, so either the step is wider than the sheet traces it or the camera's depth is wrong at the rear (its solve: +-3 m)
the rear section's door: the print's head reads about 1.7 m over grade (y 730 px), its foot hidden by the fence; the build's plain door stands 2.1 m from grade, about 8 px higher at its head
the oriel on the main south wall just in front of the rear section (x 505-527 px, about 4.0-6.6 m over grade, under a small roof): not built
the picket fence along the open ground to the south, and the builders' stone and barrels on the walk
differences.how: the fence is the lot's, not the house's, and is not built here; the debris is the photograph's day in 1889

differences.what: colour and tone: the photograph is monochrome; its stone reads mid-grey and rock-faced, the south wall's brick lighter
differences.how: the stone is K02's brownstone on the Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology, not yet a source record); L-k01-1625-mcbirney-tudor-2432
